subject: Post-demo architect recapture: credentials, routing, embeddings & toolchain next steps
messages:

Subject: Post-demo architect recapture: credentials, routing, embeddings & toolchain next steps

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great discussion. Per our call I wanted to capture the technical options we discussed so your engineering team can weigh tradeoffs and pick a guarded path forward. High level asks from Aurelia: low-latency inference (sub-200ms P95 for chat), deterministic embeddings for semantic search, and strict key rotation + auditability for regulators.

Summary of recommended options (short):
- Auth: short-lived JWT with service account issuance for server-to-server + scoped API keys for low-risk internal services. Avoid long-lived static keys for production caller flows.
- Rotation: automated rotation via KMS/HSM with a 30-day enforced rotation window; token lifetime 15 minutes for issued JWTs, refreshable by server service accounts.
- Routing: split by latency needs — fast-path (Redwood Dedicated, pinned model) vs fallback (hosted with quantized variant). Use header-based routing (x-rw-priority) to select path.
- SDK setup: use our Node/Python SDK Quickstart (attached notes) with an init call that wires credential provider chain (env var -> workload identity -> instance metadata).
- Embeddings & rerankers: store canonical embedding vectors with stable vectorization config (model + normalize steps) and include reranker as a staged model in the pipeline to avoid online cold-starts.
- Structured output/tool calling: prefer function/tool schema publishing in the model route; enforce JSON schema validation server-side.

Next steps I propose:
1) Aurelia engineering confirms preferred auth pattern (API keys only vs JWT + service accounts) this week.
2) Redwood sends a short integration diagram + sample config (attached).
3) Technical working session with Ben and Kimberly next Tue (30 min) to walk SDK init and rotation flows.
4) Procurement contact loops in to align on SOC2 evidence and contract-side rotation SLAs.

Attachments: integration-diagram-v2.png, jwt-rotation-schedule.xlsx, redwood-sdk-quickstart-notes.pdf

Thanks, Soojin — this is helpful and mirrors our internal concerns. A few clarifying points from our side:
- Procurement will want explicit language about key rotation frequency in the SOW. 30-day rotation is our baseline; we may ask for 14 days if tokens are long-lived.
- We prefer server-to-server JWTs for production inference calls from our backend, but we also have a few analytics microservices that will use API keys.
- For embeddings: reproducibility is critical — we need a pinned model + normalization pipeline documented so future re-embeds match prior vectors.

Can you and Ben map out the exact API call flow for: (1) service account generates short-lived JWT; (2) call to Redwood /v1/chat with header-based routing; (3) fallback behavior when Dedicated pool is saturated? A picture + sample curl snippets would be great.

Oliver — quick technical sketch below and a few actionables. I'll bring code samples to the working session.

API call flow (high-level):
1) Service account obtains signed JWT from Aurelia KMS/HSM (or via Workload Identity Federation) with claims: iss=aur-svc-account, aud=https://api.redwood.com/, exp=now+900s, scope=inference:generate.
2) Backend calls Redwood token-exchange endpoint (POST /v1/token/exchange) with the signed JWT to receive a short-lived bearer (15m) scoped to the customer project. This step enables centralized revocation and short lifetimes.
3) Inference call: POST /v1/chat -> Authorization: Bearer <redwood-token> and header X-RW-PRIORITY: fast-path. Redwood router checks customer capacity, model pin, and routes to Dedicated pool if available.
4) Fallback: if Dedicated capacity cannot accept the request within 30ms, router reissues to hosted quantized variant with lower cost and slightly higher latency; request attaches routing-metadata so we can re-play for logs.

Sample curl (pseudo):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer <redwood-token>" -H "X-RW-PRIORITY: fast-path" -d '{"model":"rw-chat-large-2026","input":"Hey — summarize transaction 9412"}'

Notes on rotation & audit:
- If Aurelia uses their KMS to sign JWTs, Redwood accepts and validates signatures and maintains token usage logs per token id.
- We recommend a 30-day key rotation on signing keys; token lifetime remains short (15m) so compromise window is minimal.

Embeddings recommendation: pin model (embed-stable-1) and persist normalization steps (lowercase, strip-punct, unicode-normalize). We'll provide a canonical test set you can re-run to verify determinism.

Attachments: I'll update the jwt-rotation-schedule.xlsx with the exact exchange endpoints and sample payloads before the Tue session.
